intro: This branch trains careful thinking: spotting and continuing patterns, sorting things by what they have in common, and reasoning from clues. These habits of noticing and explaining sit underneath all later math.

I.5.01.what: Copying a repeating pattern of colors or shapes exactly.

levels.a: Copies a pattern of two colors taking turns, like purple, blue, purple, blue.
levels.b: Copies a pattern of two shapes taking turns.
levels.c: Copies a pattern where one item comes once and the next twice, like red, blue, blue.
levels.d: Copies a pattern of three different items, like red, yellow, blue.

I.5.02.what: Working out what comes next in a repeating pattern.

levels.a: Says what comes next when two items take turns.
levels.b: Says what comes next in a pattern like square, square, hexagon.
levels.c: Says what comes next in a pattern of three different items.
levels.d: Picks out the part of a pattern that keeps repeating.
levels.e: Counts how many of one item appear in the first few places of a pattern.
levels.f: Works out which item comes far ahead, such as the 17th, without drawing them all.

I.5.03.what: Understanding that a pattern follows a rule, and using that rule to check and compare patterns.

levels.a: Tells a real pattern from a random row, using two kinds of item.
levels.b: The same using three kinds of item.
levels.c: Finds the one spot where a pattern has a mistake.
levels.d: Matches two patterns that follow the same rule with different items.

I.5.04.what: Understanding patterns that grow each step, like towers that get one block taller each time.

levels.a: Says how tall the next tower is when each grows by 1.
levels.b: Says how tall the next tower is when each grows by 2.
levels.c: Predicts a tower several steps ahead, not just the next one.
levels.d: Describes the rule, such as "add 1 each time."

I.5.05.what: Finding the rule in a list of numbers that goes up by the same amount each time.

levels.a: Continues a list that goes up by 1.
levels.b: Continues a list that goes up by 2.
levels.c: Continues a list that goes up by 5 or by 10.
levels.d: Finds a missing number in the middle of the list.
levels.e: Finds the rule and fills in two missing numbers, in lists going up or down.
levels.f: Spots a hidden rule, like adding 2 then 3 in turn, or adding one more each time.

I.5.06.what: Sorting things into groups by one feature, such as color, shape or size.

levels.a: Puts a new item in the right group when things are sorted by color.
levels.b: The same when things are sorted by shape.
levels.c: The same when things are sorted by size.
levels.d: Looks at sorted groups and says what the sorting rule was.

I.5.07.what: Sorting things by two features at once, such as items that are both purple and square.

levels.a: Finds items that match two features, like purple squares.
levels.b: Places a shape in two overlapping circles, such as "red" and "stars."
levels.c: Spots the one item that doesn't belong with the others, and why.
levels.d: Works out a two-part sorting rule from examples.

I.5.08.what: Telling odd numbers from even numbers: even numbers split into pairs with none left over.

levels.a: Groups objects into pairs and counts the pairs.
levels.b: Knows that one left over after pairing means the number is odd.
levels.c: Lists the even numbers up to 20 by counting in twos.
levels.d: Says whether any number is odd or even by looking at its last digit.

I.5.09.what: Looking closely to see what is the same and what is different between things.

levels.a: Spots and counts the differences between two pictures.
levels.b: Finds the item that exactly matches in color, shape and size.
levels.c: Says which feature is different between two shapes.
levels.d: Chooses the sentence that correctly describes what two shapes share.

I.5.10.what: Deciding whether a statement is true or false, and saying why.

levels.a: Checks statements about a picture, like "there are 3 purple shapes."
levels.c: Corrects a false statement by finding the right answer.
levels.d: Chooses the reason that shows why a statement is false.

I.5.11.what: Deciding whether a statement is always true, sometimes true or never true, and backing it up with examples.

levels.a: Judges statements about shapes, like "a rectangle has 5 sides."
levels.c: Finds an example that fits a description.
levels.d: Finds one example that breaks a claim (a counterexample).

I.5.12.what: Following "if this, then that" rules and working out what must happen.

levels.a: Follows everyday if–then rules, like "if the light is red, cars stop."
levels.b: Uses if–then rules about numbers to answer yes or no.
levels.c: Follows a two-way rule, such as "if less than 13, add 5; if not, take 3."
levels.d: Tests a rule and finds the example that breaks it.

I.5.13.what: Solving small logic puzzles, using a grid to track clues about who has what.

levels.a: Solves a two-person, two-item puzzle from one clue.
levels.c: Combines several clues, needing all of them to reach the answer.
levels.d: Chooses which conclusion must be true from the clues.

I.5.14.what: Putting people or things in order using clues like "taller than" or "first in line."

levels.a: Uses a taller-or-shorter clue to compare two people.
levels.b: Uses first-and-last clues to find who is in the middle.
levels.c: Combines two clues to order three people.
levels.d: Orders people using number clues, like "4 more than" or "2 fewer than."
levels.e: Uses a 'not' clue, like 'Ann was not first', to order three runners.
levels.f: Orders four runners from several clues, including 'right after'.

I.5.15.what: Finding a mystery number from clues, and learning which clues are useful.

levels.a: Finds the number from bigger-than and smaller-than clues.
levels.b: Uses an odd-or-even clue to narrow it down.
levels.c: Combines two clues, like "between 70 and 80" and "ends in 8."
levels.d: Chooses a set of clues that points to just one number.
levels.e: Finds the number using three clues together, such as range, odd or even, and digits.
levels.f: Solves a riddle about a two-digit number's digits, such as their sum and difference.
